items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: Capitaine de Chivarria was for Spanish... Capitaine de Chivarria was a Spaniard.

ctx.x: That's when we get out of the way. How many different languages could you read? Did you read German to you?

They read it to me. I was like all young people, foolish, giggling, wouldn't pay attention, wouldn't. But, you know, W.W. King. Yes. Gracie King. Yes. You know, they had a class all the week, every other day I believe, where Herman Gessner, which the one teaching there must be his grandson, and then Mrs. Verar and Charles Gaiare. Oh, yes. Mrs. Gerard and Charles Gaiare was French, and Capitaine de Chivarria was for Spanish, and Herman Gessner was German. So every other day they had a class, ladies would be there,…
You can understand Spanish then too? A little. Were there many Spanish people in the city when you were young that you remember?

items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: One day it would be Capitán de Chivarria, that was for the Spanish. And nothing but Spanish. And they speak it to me and I dig it like a little young crazy thing, you know.

ctx.x: And was, Bill says, was French the only language you could read in?

Well, it's the language that I could read with more facilité, you know. Yes. But I read because, you see, old Mrs. W. W. King, Grace King. Her mother? Huh? Grace King's mother? Grace King's mother. I worked there. And there they used to have classes every three, about four days in the week. One day it would be Capitán de Chivarria, that was for the Spanish. And nothing but Spanish. And they speak it to me and I dig it like a little young crazy thing, you know. I wasn't twenty years old. Then one day it was Herman…
And which language did Guayari teach?
